children: By Samantha Kroontje, Alicia McElhaney and Andrew Scurria

Creditors set to drive potential restructuring talks with JetBlue Airways agreed to improve the terms of their cooperation agreement for other signatories, according to people familiar with the matter.

The airline, advised by law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell, has been struggling with cash burn and elevated operating costs because of high oil prices while addressing roughly $8.5 billion in debt and lease obligations.

A group of creditors hired law firm Akin Gump and financial adviser PJT Partners last month and formed a cooperation group to prepare for potential negotiations with the company, the people said. Key investors set to lead negotiations on behalf of the co-op group — including Franklin Templeton, Pimco and BlackRock — were positioned to receive better terms than other members in the same group, the people said.

A separate group of creditors looking to rival the majority group has organized with law firm Hogan Lovells Cadwalader, the people said. The group, which held a minority position in JetBlue's bonds and term loan, has grown large enough to potentially block transactions in a bankruptcy scenario, the people said.

Akin revised the co-op agreement on Sunday to allow members outside the steering group to receive improved terms in a potential restructuring while still securing additional value for the steering committee of lenders, the people said.
Franklin Templeton declined to comment. Representatives for Akin, PJT, Davis Polk and the other creditors didn't immediately respond to requests seeking comment.

A JetBlue spokesperson said the company "can't comment on private agreements between creditors or market speculation," adding that it had roughly $7 billion in unencumbered assets at the end of the third quarter.
New York-based JetBlue reported revenue growth and highlighted that it ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity and better-than-expected results in the quarter.
JetBlue's stock has lost about 42% in value since the start of August.
